newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland releases German bomb attack suspect.
newsitem.headline: Ireland releases German bomb attack suspect.

text.p: Ireland has rejected a German application for the extradition of James Anthony Corry who is wanted by German authorities in connection with a mortar bomb attack on a British Army barracks in Osnabruck last June.
Justice ministry officials said on Wednesday that Ireland had been forced to release the wanted man because Belfast-born Corry had declared his Irish citizenship.
There are no reciprocal arrangements in place between Ireland and Germany for the extradition of Irish nationals.

A statement from the justice ministry said that legislation dictated that "extradition shall not be granted where the person claimed is a citizen of Ireland, unless the relevant extradition provisions otherwise provide."
Corry was arrested in the Irish Republic in November and appeared in an Irish District Court for proceedings relating to the German extradition bid.

The 27-year old actor had been remanded in custody pending further court hearings but justice minister Nora Owen freed him on Tuesday after being presented with a declaration of his Irish citizenship.
Corry is one of five people wanted in connection with the Osnabruck attack in which no one was hurt but a number of buildings were damaged.

Roisin McAliskey, the pregnant daughter of Bernadette McAliskey, who from 1969-74 was a member of the British parliament for a Northern Ireland constituency, is currently in custody in Britain pending the hearing of an application for her extradition to Germany in connection with the same attack.
